newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares seen quiet on scattered support.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares seen quiet on scattered support.

text.p: Leading Russian shares were varied in early trade on Tuesday and traders said they expected another slow day on mixed quiet support while Western investors worried about volatile European markets and looked to less liquid stock.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index opened slightly off at 355.26 after closing on Monday at 355.46.

"There's been a lot of upheaval in Europe market because of the EMU situation," said Martin Diggle, director at Brunswick, referring to uncertainty over European Monetary Union (EMU) in the wake of a Socialist win in France this weekend.
"It could be that a lot of investors have been focusing on the volatility in the European markets rather than on emerging markets in Eastern Europe."

Traders said they expected low volumes and little price movement on the market, which has hovered at current levels for several days now as interest has turned to second tier shares, although they saw gentle support for some individual stocks.
"There are quiet, non-aggressive buyers on the market -- as soon as they've bought, the price sags a bit until the next one buys," said Dmitry Yershov, head of trading at Alfa Capital.

Yershov saw interest from both Western and domestic players, and noted activity in oil producer LUKoil, which firmed to $14.99 from $14.98 at 0830 GMT, and national savings bank Sberbank which rose to $147.8 from $143.9.
National utility UES firmed to $0.3140 after $0.3135 previously. International long-distance provider Rostelekom rose to $3.79 from $3.76 previously.
Rostelekom said it would pay a 475.61 rouble dividend on preferred shares with a face value of 2.5 roubles, against 475.61 roubles in 1995. It again omitted a dividend on ordinary shares.
